label: input token l at original position >= 4
explanation: Fires exactly when the input token is the letter l during the original (pre-<DEL>) phase at position t >= 4 (dev P=R=1.0). Never fires on l at positions 0-3, on any other token, on the delimiter, or in the copy phase (including when l is fed back as a copy-phase input). Magnitude increases with position: about 0.2 of max at t=4, about 0.5 at t=5, about 0.7 at t=6, near max at t=7-8 (checked against mass-share-per-count by t and the quartile examples). Preceding tokens, first token, L and digit count do not modulate it noticeably.

issues: None found. On the test split, misses reports 0 missed activations and 0 false positives. Precision, recall, F1 and mass recall are all 1.0, and coverage is 1.0 in every activation quartile.

The dev profile backs the factual claims. The feature fires only on in_tok=l and only in the original phase: delimiter and copy phase have 0 activations, and recall_idx >= 0 has 0. It never fires at t=0-3, while at orig_idx 4-8 the rate stays flat at about 0.033, which is about 1/30, the base rate of the letter l.

The magnitude claim checks out. Mean activation per t (mass share divided by count), relative to t=8, is about 0.22 at t=4, 0.53 at t=5, 0.78 at t=6, 0.94 at t=7 and 1.0 at t=8. This matches the stated growth with position.
The rising rate with L, and the zero rate at L=3-4, come only from how many positions >= 4 a sequence has. They are not an independent dependence on L.
